clearedSpotChecks.check: The five Salvador sweeper targets (0xe4C4...1EC6, 0x5392...962C, 0xc91e...9b60, 0x3f70...1Ffa, 0x5227...2f8c) against every call the PoolManager can make to them after block 98,688,600, with the sweeper code from bor develop params/config.go placed by state override; plus their current balance, code, nonce and PoolManager claims.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched https://raw.githubusercontent.com/0xPolygon/bor/develop/params/config.go. Line 478 sets SalvadorBlock to 98,688,600 and line 476 leaves Hampi nil. The block alloc at key 98688600 writes the same sweeper runtime to the five addresses; its dispatcher only knows selectors 0x35faa416 and 0x78ed5d81 and ends in a revert for any other calldata, including empty calldata, so native transfers, transfer(address,uint256) and balanceOf all revert as the research says. The research only read claim ids 0 and WPOL. I widened that: eth_getLogs on https://polygon.gateway.tenderly.co over blocks 0 to latest for the PoolManager 0x6736...5cd6 returned no ERC-6909 Transfer event with any of the five as from or to, and no OperatorSet with any of them as owner (an unfiltered query over the same range answered that it exceeds 20,000 results, so the endpoint does search the full range). No claim of any id was ever held by them. EOAs cannot hold positions because unlock calls back msg.sender (src/PoolManager.sol unlock path), so no position is keyed to them. Code read: native take uses call and reverts with NativeTransferFailed on failure (src/types/Currency.sol:44-52), ERC-20 transfer requires success and a true or empty return (src/types/Currency.sol:54-87), sync calls balanceOfSelf which reverts with the call (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, src/types/Currency.sol:90-95). The code write is a chain governance action (F-134); no ordinary-account path follows from it.

clearedSpotChecks.check: The same 185,529 vectors and script sets 1 and 2 on BNB Chain with every eth_call carrying blockOverrides time 1,796,697,100 (100 s after Jenner), on Geth v1.8.2 and reth-bsc v0.1.4-hotfix-23b510f.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I queried precompile 0x70 myself: with blockOverrides time 0x6b176c0c both https://bsc-dataseed1.bnbchain.org (web3_clientVersion Geth/v1.8.2-4e1c8247-20261104/linux-amd64/go1.26.10) and https://bsc-rpc.publicnode.com (reth-bsc/v0.1.4-hotfix-23b510f/linux) return 0x...1a2537e0ee0 = 1,796,697,100,000, and without the override both return 0x. The override therefore does put both builds under Jenner rules. bsc develop params/config.go line 256 reads JennerTime newUint64(1796697000). The wrapper jenner_run.py keeps any state override at params index 2 and adds the block override at index 3, and all eight logs in out/jen_*.log show 0 mismatches, 250/250 and 300/300 identical. One limit: eth_call under a time override exercises the post-Jenner opcode and precompile set, but it does not exercise block-level changes such as BEP-703 that act only in block import; these do not change what a call returns, so the clearing holds for the PoolManager arithmetic.
